subject: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging
body:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging

Naomi — looping you in for security/compliance sign-off on the Suggestions view (beta).

Primary question from Marissa/Dylan: do the savings/risk details expose sensitive usage patterns (volume, route names, model mix) in a way that changes our threat model? We’re trying to keep the beta read-only, allowlisted, and scoped to the tenant.

Can you review and confirm requirements for:
1) RBAC scope for viewing Suggestions + suggestion detail
2) Audit logging granularity (view list vs open detail)
3) Any suppression/rounding requirements for low-traffic routes

Attached:
- Suggestions_Beta_Security_Review_Checklist_v3.pdf
- Suggestions_UI_Data_Elements_RBAC_Matrix.xlsx

If helpful, the implementation work is tracking under ENG-2408 and the audit log PR is redwood/pr-18695.

Thanks,
Marcus
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging

Thanks — taking a look now.

Framing: savings/risk detail is derived from cost + usage telemetry, so it can be sensitive in two ways:
- intra-tenant: a user without appropriate permissions can infer product usage patterns (route names, traffic shape, spend)
- cross-tenant: any scoping bug becomes higher impact because the data is “analytics-like,” not just config

Initial position (pending Kaitlyn confirmation on authz wiring): we can ship beta if the following are true:

RBAC
- Suggestions list + detail must be behind an explicit permission (not just “can view routes”). Proposed: console.optimize.suggestions:read.
- Permission should be limited to Workspace Admin + Billing Admin equivalents, and any custom role that explicitly includes the permission.
- For Dedicated/Private, keep consistent with whatever role gates usage/cost dashboards today (if different, we need a deliberate decision).

Audit logging
- Must log:
  a) suggestions.list_view (or equivalent) — whenever the page fetches list data
  b) suggestions.detail_view — whenever a suggestion id is opened
- Include actor_user_id, workspace_id, org_id, suggestion_id (for detail), timestamp, and request_id.
- Do NOT include raw savings values/rationale text in the audit log payload (keep audit records metadata-only).

Data minimization / suppression
- I recommend we suppress or bucket any “basis of estimate” fields that could reveal exact traffic volumes for low-traffic routes.
  - Example: if a route has <N requests/day (or <X tokens/day), show “insufficient data” instead of exposing token counts.
  - If we must show counts, round to coarse buckets (e.g., 10k tokens, 50k tokens, 100k tokens) and avoid per-hour breakdown.

Can you confirm whether the UI shows any of the following today:
- exact tokens/day per route
- p95 latency headroom numbers per route
- exact cache hit rate values per route

If it does, I want to tighten the fields for beta.

Naomi
Security/Compliance Product
Redwood Inference


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:11 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging

Naomi — super helpful.

Answering your questions based on current spec/implementation:
- We do NOT show exact tokens/day in the list. In detail drawer we show a “basis of estimate” section with:
  - baseline window (e.g., “last 7 days”)
  - traffic eligibility note (e.g., “sufficient traffic for estimate”) OR “insufficient telemetry”
  - optional values: cache hit-rate confidence + sampling coverage (not raw hit rate)
- We show projected savings in $/1M tokens and “estimated monthly impact” as a dollar range.
- We show risk level (Low/Medium/High) + rationale bullets (text), but not raw p95 latency headroom numbers.

On suppression: We can enforce “insufficient data” display if the backend doesn’t return a baseline / confidence above threshold. We already have that path for missing telemetry.

On permissions: today the page is behind feature flag + allowlist. We can also add the explicit console.optimize.suggestions:read permission check.

Logan (cc’d) owns analytics; he can confirm we’re not emitting raw savings numbers in audit logs.

If there’s any specific N/X threshold you want for “low traffic,” we can implement server-side in suggestions-service and keep UI dumb.

Marissa
PM, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


---

From: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 1:26 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging

Confirming authz approach:

- We can add a dedicated permission string: console.optimize.suggestions.read (naming can follow our convention).
- We’ll gate both list and detail endpoints in the Console BFF and in suggestions-service (defense in depth).
- Tenant scoping: suggestions-service requires workspace_id from the caller’s token context; no workspace_id accepted from query params.
- We will also enforce that suggestion_id lookups validate workspace_id matches (no “guessable id” leak).

Audit logging: PR redwood/pr-18695 logs a “SuggestionsAccessed” event today (workspace_id, actor_user_id, operation=list|detail, suggestion_id when present). No payload fields.

One thing to decide: should Billing Admin have access by default? Currently billing roles can see Usage/Cost pages in Console. Aligning would mean yes.

Kaitlyn
Security Engineering (AuthZ/Tenancy)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 2:03 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging

On the analytics/audit side:
- Audit logs: agree with “metadata-only.” We won’t include savings values, rationale bullets, baselines, or confidence.
- Product analytics events (ENG-2409 / redwood/pr-18690): we do have “suggestion_opened” etc. These events are privacy-safe and will include only:
  - workspace_id
  - suggestion_id
  - suggestion_type (batching|caching)
  - risk_level (low|medium|high)
  - estimate_version (e.g., v1)
No token counts, no $ values.

Re: low-traffic suppression — we already have a concept of “coverage” and “min_samples.” We can tune the backend so that if min_samples isn’t met, the suggestion is either not generated or generated with “insufficient data” and without savings numbers.

Logan
Telemetry & Analytics
Redwood Inference


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kaitlyn Nguyen <kaitlyn.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: Console Suggestions (beta) — savings/risk details + RBAC/audit logging

Decision: Approved for beta with requirements below.

1) RBAC (required)
- Add explicit permission gate for viewing Suggestions list + detail: console.optimize.suggestions.read.
- Default allow: Workspace Admin + Billing Admin (to match existing cost/usage visibility). Any expansion beyond that needs a follow-up review.
- Enforce permission at BOTH layers (Console BFF + suggestions-service). Kaitlyn’s plan sounds good.

2) Audit logging (required)
- Log list access + detail access (separately).
- Audit payload must remain metadata-only (no $ values, no baseline values, no rationale text).
- Retention and access controls should match existing Console audit logs.

3) Low-traffic / sensitive inference (required)
- Backend must suppress savings numbers and basis-of-estimate details when min_samples/coverage threshold not met.
- In those cases, UI should display “Insufficient data to estimate savings” (or equivalent) and avoid showing any numeric counts.

4) Cross-tenant risk (required)
- Confirm suggestion_id lookup validates workspace_id ownership.
- Add a unit/integration test that attempts to fetch a suggestion_id from a different workspace and asserts 404.

If you want a concrete threshold for (3), I’m fine with the backend owning it as long as it’s deterministic and documented (e.g., “minimum telemetry coverage required for estimates” in internal docs). Just avoid showing a precise “tokens processed” number anywhere in the Suggestions UI for beta.

Please reply-all once the permission string is finalized so I can note it in the compliance tracker.

Naomi
Security/Compliance Product
Redwood Inference
